OEM Fleet Recall Propagation

RelationalAI demo for a major European luxury OEM. A 5-act RelationalAI demo against the sales-engineering Snowflake account.

Engines: cars_logic_l, cars_prescriptive_m Database: CARS_DEMO.FLEET Agent: cars

Why this demo exists - non-expert primer

🚨The customer problem

A Tier-1 supplier flags a defect on Tuesday morning. By end of day the after-sales lead at a major car manufacturer needs concrete answers: how many VINs are affected, which owners we must write to, which service centres are about to be overrun, and whether we can finish the work before the regulator's window expires.

Today this conversation spans six different systems: a parts catalogue, an as-built BOM database, a dealer-network capacity sheet, a parts logistics spreadsheet, an owner-notification ledger, and a senior manager's spreadsheet of "always pull these VINs first" rules.

5 active campaigns · 121 open recalls · 19 already past their SLA

🧩Why it's hard

The connections that matter cut across systems: supplier → part → bill-of-materials cohort → VIN → owner → service centre → region. Each step is a different team and a different join key. The "always prioritise VINs with a prior collision" rule lives in one person's head.

Doing this in SQL alone means manually re-deriving the cascade every time and re-hardcoding the priority rule into every report. Doing it with bespoke scripts means three or four hand-stitched data products that drift apart within a quarter.

Touch six systems, get the answer wrong 5-10% of the time, ship in 3 days

⚡How RelationalAI helps

One ontology over the same Snowflake data captures the relationships, the rules, and the policies in one place. Five different reasoners then share that ontology:

Rules audit the open recalls, a Graph reasoner walks the supplier→VIN cascade, a Heuristic ranks urgency, a Prescriptive MIP schedules jobs to centres, and a Persistent-rule capability lets the operator write the priority policy into the ontology so every downstream reasoner respects it without redeployment.

Same model, five reasoners, sub-minute answers, the policy survives

🏗️What the alternative looks like

Without RAI you'd assemble: a data engineer to wire the six joins, a data scientist to build the urgency model, an OR analyst to formulate the LP, and a senior product manager to keep the priority rules in a runbook. Three weeks of work, four maintenance owners, and the policies don't propagate when the data changes.

The talk track shows the same question landed in the agent that touches one model, in natural language, in under 90 seconds per question.

3 weeks + 4 owners → one ontology, one schema, an agent that answers in natural language

What you'll see - one ontology, five reasoners

The demo runs against CARS_DEMO.FLEET on the sales-engineering Snowflake account. 325 vehicles, 762 service events, 254 recall assignments across 5 active campaigns. A single PyRel ontology backs every act below; the Cortex agent cars answers all the same questions in natural language.

The 5 acts - one slide per reasoner

Rules Act 1 - Recall SLA compliance audit

In plain languageLook at every Open recall whose owner-notification age has slipped past the campaign's regulator-defined completion window. The rule lives in the ontology as a derived predicate; the audit query just counts.

Per NHTSA 49 CFR 577 / KBA Rueckruf, Code-1 and Code-2 recalls must complete within the campaign window measured from owner-notification date. The rule lives in the ontology as SLABreachedRecall - a derived concept that re-runs against the current data automatically.

Speaker beat: Expected output: 19 SLA-breached Open recalls. Leader: IBS-2024-A (Continental MK C1 brake-booster firmware, 8 cases). Severity Code 1 cases (HVB-2024-A, 7) matter most per VIN. By centre, Cologne / Hamburg / Munich are the most exposed.

Paste into Snowflake Intelligence

Which open recalls are past their completion window? Show me the count by campaign.

Expected result. Bars / rows / shape.
What changes if the audience disputes a number
Both the rule and the result reproduce from the ontology. Run data/out/cars_demo_validation.sql in Snowsight to confirm the underlying SQL counts; if the numbers drift, the data has changed under us and bash data/load_to_snowflake.sh rebuilds from seed=42.

Graph Act 2 - Continental MK C1 defect cascade

In plain languageA supplier flags a part. The ontology walks the cascade from supplier to part to bill-of-materials node to affected VIN to owner to nearest service centre in a single query - the join that today takes six handoffs across six teams.

Supplier-to-VIN propagation today is a six-system stitch (BMW AIR -> iLEAD -> dealer-network DB). The ontology walks it in a single PyRel query that joins supplier -> part -> bom_node -> vehicle -> owner -> service centre.

Speaker beat: Expected output: 67 affected VINs across three plant-date cohorts (Munich, Regensburg, Spartanburg). Regional rollup: EU 53, NA 12, LATAM 2. Top centres: Hamburg, Frankfurt, Berlin, Munich. The Sankey shows the cascade visually.

Paste into Snowflake Intelligence

Continental flagged a defect in the MK C1 brake booster ECU. Show me every VIN affected, broken down by region.

Graph Act 2b - Vehicle cohort communities (Louvain)

In plain languageSame data as Act 2, structural view. Two VINs share a tie when they share a BOM node. Louvain - a community-detection algorithm - finds the natural cohorts: the groups of vehicles that will move together if a supplier widens any defect notice. Operations now sees portfolio risk, not per-campaign tickets.

A graph reasoner running Louvain on the BOM-sharing graph identifies the 4 natural exposure cohorts among ~190 BOM-participating VINs. The largest cluster is the Continental IBS exposure (Munich + Regensburg + Spartanburg X-series + G21 LCI). The second clusters Dingolfing iX / i7 EVs around the Samsung SDI HV battery campaign.

Speaker beat: pivot here from Act 2 when the audience wants the picture, not the table. The force-directed Plotly view colours nodes by community and sizes them by degree. Hover any node for VIN / model / plant / fuel / mileage / community / degree / campaign count / open recalls / accident type.

Paste into Snowflake Intelligence

Run Louvain community detection on the vehicle-cohort graph - two VINs share an edge when they share a BOM node. Show me the clusters and their dominant model.

Louvain is non-deterministic. Community labels may shuffle between runs; the cohort sizes and dominant-model-per-cohort are stable.
Why this isn't just a fancy chart
The communities are derived structure on the same ontology that backs Act 1's SLA audit, Act 3's urgency score, Act 4's MIP, and Act 5's policy rule. Adding a downstream rule like "alert when more than N priority VINs land in the same community" is one PyRel derived property - it lights up in every reasoner that touches the model.

Heuristic Act 3 - Per-VIN urgency ranking (top 20)

In plain languageOf the ~120 Open recall jobs, give me the top 20 to act on this week. The score weights mileage (how much the car is driven), notification age (how long the owner has had the letter), prior accident severity, and distance to the nearest equipped centre.

Score = w1*mileage + w2*notification_age + w3*accident_severity + w4*distance_to_centre. All weights and all inputs are PyRel-derived properties. Auditable, defensible, reproducible across runs.

Speaker beat: Top of the queue mixes Regensburg X1 M35i + iX1 units with high mileage and prior collisions, plus Dingolfing iX / i7 EVs from the HVB campaign. Visible accident_severity column makes the safety argument explicit.

Note: the predictive (GNN) reasoner is still preview. This is a deterministic fit-score expressed entirely as PyRel-derived properties - auditable and defensible to insurance / compliance reviewers in a way a black-box model is not.

Paste into Snowflake Intelligence

Rank the open recall jobs by urgency. Weight mileage, notification age, prior accident severity, and distance to the nearest equipped centre. Show me the top 20.

Prescriptive Act 4 - MIP: assign recall jobs to centres x 4 weeks

In plain languageSchedule the next four weeks of recall work. Every open job goes to exactly one centre in exactly one week. Respect technician hours, parts on hand, and tooling certification. Minimise total weighted lateness. A mixed-integer program (HiGHS solver) finds the optimum.

HiGHS MIP. Decision: x[recall, centre, week] binary. Constraints: per-centre weekly technician hours, per-centre per-campaign per-week parts stock, tooling-certification eligibility (HV / IBS / body shop). Objective: sum(x * urgency * (week-1)).

Speaker beat: Expected: OPTIMAL in under 60 seconds (warm). All 121 Open jobs scheduled. The binding constraint in practice is parts stock on the IBS campaign (Continental can't ship enough booster ECUs in 4 weeks). EU jobs cluster in DE centres; US in Spartanburg / Dallas / NYC / LA. Budget 2-3 min of dead air for the solver - use it to narrate.

Paste into Snowflake Intelligence

Schedule the next four weeks of open recall jobs to service centres. Minimise urgency-weighted lateness, respect tooling certifications and parts stock. How many jobs deferred past week 4?

Persistent rule Act 5 - Persistent rule: prior-accident VINs go to week 1 or 2

In plain languageThe senior recall manager says "VINs that already had a collision must go to weeks 1 or 2; we absorb the slip elsewhere." Today that rule lives in her spreadsheet. We write it into the ontology in ~10 lines of PyRel and re-solve. Every downstream reasoner picks it up without code changes.

The rule is captured once as RecallAssignment.priority_flag on the ontology. Adding it triggers a re-solve under the new constraint sum(assign at week>=3) == 0 for priority VINs. The rule survives the session - the next agent / SE / human inherits it.

Speaker beat: Expected: re-solve OPTIMAL in under 60s. 4-6 reassignments (priority VINs move into weeks 1 or 2; other jobs absorb the slip). Total weighted lateness rises ~5-10% - the rule trades raw efficiency for safety, as intended. Live-add the rule. Re-solve. Audience sees the answer flip - and crucially the rule stays in the ontology for everything else that reads from it.

Paste into Snowflake Intelligence

Add this rule to the ontology and re-solve: any open recall on a VIN with a prior collision in the last three years must be scheduled in week 1 or 2. Show me what changed.

The closing one-liner
"We just moved institutional knowledge from a person to a data model." Pause. That's the demo.

If things break - demo-day triage

  • Engine not READY. .venv/bin/rai reasoners list to confirm. The gate auto-resumes them, but it can take 3-5 minutes cold.
  • Stale notebook in Snowsight. bash data/upload_snowsight_notebook.sh re-uploads.
  • Agent answering with stale schema. .venv/bin/python -m agent.deploy update refreshes sprocs without re-registering.
  • Solver returning INFEASIBLE. Not a runtime problem - the formulation drifted. Check data/out/cars_demo_validation.sql first; if data changed under you, regenerate. Otherwise the formulation needs /rai-prescriptive-problem-formulation.
  • Snowflake credentials. snow connection test -c rai. Profile lives in ~/.snowflake/connections.toml.
  • Cortex agent dies mid-demo. Fall back to .venv/bin/python -m agent.deploy chat "<question>" from the terminal. Slower (~90s per answer) but functional.
